core_obligations: Both sides as compatible systems (proof lines 8182-8192): a morphism from a presheaf into the direct image of a set is described as a compatible system of maps from the values times the values of the functor into the set; a morphism from the stalk into the set is described as a rule on triples constant on equivalent triples, which the author observes is the same thing as such a compatible system; the two descriptions coincide.
proof_roadmap: Describe a morphism into the direct image as a compatible system of maps.
Describe a morphism out of the stalk as a compatible system of maps using the description of the stalk.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for any set-valued functor the direct image on presheaves is right adjoint to the stalk functor (statement lines 8174-8179). The proof is a short but complete argument: a morphism from a presheaf into the direct image of a set is a compatible system of maps from the values times the values of the functor into the set, and the description of the stalk shows that a morphism out of the stalk into the set is the same kind of compatible system (proof lines 8182-8192), which gives the asserted bijection. The non-formal content is the comparison of the two descriptions. The claim is H1: a one-step comparison with its inputs named.
